sections.sectionSummaryBrief: After explaining the superiority of anointing oil, the maamar explains that oil for illumination (the Chanukah miracle) is even higher, as the light from the oil's consumption surpasses the oil itself and even its fragrance.

translations.translation: And now, after the maamar explains
(beginning with "Baruch She'asah Nissim")
the great superiority of the anointing oil,
it explains,
that "oil for illumination"
(in which the miracle of Chanukah occurred)
is even more elevated than the anointing oil.
For the light produced from the oil
(for light comes from the consumption of the oil)
is above the oil.
And this is analogous to the fragrance that was in the anointing oil, which is above the oil.
[And furthermore,
the light produced from the oil is above even the fragrance of the oil,
as explained in the maamar].
And the difference between them is,
that the fragrance in the anointing oil is for the sake of the oil,
for through the fragrance the oil of anointing is drawn into revelation,
so that they could inaugurate the altar with it
(to make it fit for offerings and libations),
but regarding oil and light, it is the opposite,
the oil is for the sake of the light,
to the point that the oil is consumed and light is made from it.
And there is another aspect to this,
the light that comes from the consumption of the oil,
even though in its own essence it is a state of concealment,
for in addition to the nature of light
(whatever fire it may be)
to ascend to its source,
regarding this light
(that comes from the consumption of the oil),
even the oil itself is a state of concealment,
and certainly the light that comes from the consumption of the oil and is above it,
and nevertheless,
it
becomes a light that illuminates.
And moreover,
through the oil it burns gently,
a light of settled calm.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: From this, the greatness of the Chanukah miracle of the cruse of oil is understood, where the miraculous light was even more elevated yet still shone in revelation and settlement, linked to the eight days representing a drawing from the seven days of Atik into Malchus.

translations.translation: And)
From all this, the great superiority of the miracle of Chanukah, which was with the cruse of oil, is understood,
that there was only enough to light for one day, yet a miracle occurred and they lit from it for eight days,
for the light they lit from this oil,
since it was through a miracle,
is even more elevated,
and nevertheless,
this light also shone in revelation,
and with settled calm.
And this can be connected with the fact that they lit for eight days,
"The days of Chanukah are eight,"
for the matter of eight days is
(as explained in the maamar there)
the drawing down from the seven days of Atik
(a most elevated level)
into Malchus
(the source of created beings,
and through Malchus this light is drawn down in revelation even below).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: May we soon merit the coming of Moshiach, when the river will split into seven streams, alongside the eight-stringed lyre and ultimately the ten-stringed lyre of the World to Come in the eternal Third Temple, immediately.

translations.translation: A)
And may it be His will,
that very soon we merit the coming of Moshiach Tzidkeinu,
when "He will smite it into seven streams,"
and together with this, the lyre of eight strings,
and up to the lyre of the World to Come, which will have ten strings,
and this lyre will also be in the Third Holy Temple, which will be built with the coming of Moshiach Tzidkeinu
(for the Third Holy Temple will be an eternal House),
and all this very soon,
and in a manner of "immediately,"
in the language of the Rambam,
"immediately they are redeemed."
